layers.note: A herb of moist forest by streams and seeps.

heat_load.note: Favours cool, shaded aspects and ravines; scarce on hot south-west slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,200 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

sun_tolerance.note: Grows in shaded, moist woods; scarce in full sun.

coldest_c.note: A mild maritime winter: coldest-month means from about −4 °C (gone by −9 °C), as along the coast and in the lowlands west of the Cascades and Coast Mountains.

hard_freeze_c.note: Winter lows of the maritime Northwest: lows to about −24 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −32 °C.

warmest_c.note: Cool to warm summers: warmest-month means from about 13.5 to 23.5 °C; below 11 °C summers are too short for it and above 27 °C too hot.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.62, gone by 0.5.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Piggyback plant grows in moist forest from Alaska to northern California (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
